column5: Sequence diagram of indirect prompt injection: a user asks an agent to summarize a web page, the page carries a hidden instruction, and the agent calls send_email to the attacker, with the lethal trifecta of private data, untrusted content and an exfiltration channel below.

User input passes input rails, the LLM call and output rails before the response, with block, tool-argument allowlist and regenerate-or-abstain branches, plus fail-closed, fail-open and latency choices per rail.

A request passes auth and quotas, per-request classifiers and session and account behavioral signals into a risk score that serves, adds friction or blocks for review, with confirmed abuse retraining the classifiers and enforcement escalating from friction to ban.
AI incident lifecycle from detected, triaged, contained and investigated to remediated, notified and reviewed, with each review producing a new eval case that feeds detection.

Healthcare chatbot flow: emergencies go to a fixed response with human escalation, diagnosis requests get a templated triage reply, everything else goes to an LLM on approved content and an output check that passes the answer or regenerates once then falls back.

A runaway feedback loop where the model flags area A, scrutiny rises there, more incidents are recorded and training data over-represents A, beside the four data-side fixes: exploration, holdout, propensity weights and independent labels.

Sequence diagram of an appeal: the system sends a denial with reasons and an appeal link, the user appeals, a human reviewer forms their own view before seeing the model output and upholds or overturns, with legal anchors, feedback into evals and the rubber-stamping warning sign below.

Decision records holding the request, model hash, prompt version, retrieved context and reason flow with human review actions through a durable queue into an append-only WORM store that is hash-chained and indexed by user and date.

Image, audio and text go through a vision encoder, an audio encoder and a tokenizer, the projector maps encoder outputs into one interleaved token sequence, and a transformer backbone produces text or tokens for a decoder.

A 336 by 336 image is cut into 576 patches, encoded by a ViT, projected by a 2-layer MLP into 576 image tokens placed in the prompt between text tokens, and read by the LLM decoder, with the two training stages alongside.

Whisper pipeline: 16 kHz audio becomes a 30-second log-Mel window of 80 by 3,000 frames, a conv stem halves it to 1,500 frames, the encoder feeds the decoder through cross-attention, and special tokens steer language, task and timestamps.

Sequence diagram of barge-in between user, client and server: speech is detected after echo cancellation, playback stops at 2.4 s, LLM and TTS are cancelled, and only the heard part of the assistant turn is kept in history.
Photos and text are normalized, routed to OCR, a small classifier or a VLM with a JSON schema, validated against the text and business rules, and then either automated or sent to human review.

Video is indexed into keyframes and a timestamped transcript stored as segment records with embeddings, and each question retrieves the relevant segments for a VLM that answers with timestamps, beside the token budget of about 900k tokens per hour.

Uploads pass a hash match that blocks and reports known content, then extraction, per-modality classifiers and a multimodal policy model that allows or removes clear cases and sends uncertain ones to human review, with a benign image plus benign caption shown as hateful together.

The prompt and reference image are encoded and condition a diffusion transformer that denoises a noisy spacetime latent cut into patches, and a video VAE decoder turns the result into a clip that is then upscaled.

A multi-page document is narrowed to the relevant pages, each page is read by a VLM at full resolution and extracted to a schema with its page number, and the extractions are aggregated in text or code into an answer with page citations.
